details: === CONSENSUS FINDINGS === - .github/workflows/plan.yml and .github/workflows/clarify.yml (Plan failure comment handler (plan.yml) and blocked-outcome comment POST (clarify.yml)) | severity=critical | confidence=5 flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite] PROBLEM: The plan and clarify failure handlers do not write the AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1 marker that the P3 step 1 contract requires. WHY: The orchestrator's failure breaker looks for these markers before it allows a retry or escalation, so without them the breaker never trips in production and repeated plan/clarify failures can loop indefinitely. This is the same root cause as the README breaker finding below and the P3 task gap, but it is kept separate because the cited files differ. - README.md (section "Stall recovery: failure-signature breaker", the paragraph saying the markers are "written by the plan and clarify failure handlers"); also agents.d/stuck-states-p3b-stall-breaker.md line 2 and changelog.d/stuck-states-p3b-stall-breaker.md line 2; scripts/orchestrate_lib.py comment above FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_MARKER_PREFIX | severity=high | confidence=5 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5] PROBLEM: The breaker is on by default (STALL_FINGERPRINT_BREAKER_ENABLED=true in orchestrate_poll.yml) and is documented as consuming markers written by the plan/clarify failure handlers, but no workflow or script writes AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1. WHY: _failure_fingerprint_breaker_check returns early with FFB_DECISION=none on every issue and every tick, so the plan↔clarification retrigger loop still runs unbounded (until stall exhaustion) while the operator docs say it is stopped. - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22728 | severity=high | confidence=5 flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite] PROBLEM: The managed breaker passes "true" as the comments-complete flag, but the source cache comes from comments(last: 100) at line 20207, so a 100-comment window is treated as full history. WHY: A marker older than the window may be ignored (the breaker fails to trip), or an older, different marker outside the window can cause a false trip. Three reviewers checked this against the code and rejected it: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash say ffb_complete=true is set only when the cache holds fewer than 100 comments, and otherwise needs_full_history triggers the paginated read. - scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh:137-150, 216-218; .github/workflows/clarify.yml:434-442 | severity=high | confidence=5 flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna] PROBLEM: When SCRIPT_REF=stable and the stable checkout fails, clarify.yml checks out main but leaves SCRIPT_REF=stable. The staging helper accepts the unresolved ref as head_only and stages the checkout anyway, and no later step checks the exported SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_VERIFY. WHY: On the documented fallback, the stable workflow can run main's support scripts without verifying that they match SCRIPT_REF, which defeats support-ref verification. - scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh:303-311 | severity=low | confidence=4 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3] PROBLEM: The informational exclusions listing (`with excluded_list_path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as excluded_sink:`) is written inside the fatal try-block whose `except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeError)` raises `SystemExit("clarify source snapshot rejected")`. WHY: An OSError on this advisory file (ENOSPC/EACCES/EDQUOT/quota on the run_root or runner temp volume) throws away a complete, valid snapshot and fails clarify, clarify-respond, plan, check-failure-triage and unblock-judge runs with a misleading message. - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (_failure_fingerprint_breaker_apply, `if ! gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${issue_num}/comments" -f body="${ffb_body}" ...; then ... --remove-label "${FFB_LABEL}" ... return 1`) | severity=low | confidence=3 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5] PROBLEM: If GitHub applies the breaker comment but the response is lost (5xx or timeout), the handler treats the post as failed and rolls back the label, leaving an orphan trusted AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_BREAKER_V1 comment on the issue. WHY: The evaluator treats the orphan comment as the consumption point (window_start), so the markers that should have tripped the breaker are consumed, the issue keeps neither label and the legacy ladder resumes. The trip is silently lost and the issue shows a false "Repeated failure detected: automatic retries stopped" comment (bounded: two more identical failures are needed). - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22652 | severity=low | confidence=4 flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite] PROBLEM: The breaker comment POST is not marked GH_RETRY_IDEMPOTENT=true. WHY: If the POST fails on a transient 5xx or timeout after GitHub has already applied the write, a retry posts a second identical breaker comment. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and minimax_minimax-m3 rejected this: gh_retry makes one attempt for an unmarked POST create (scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1166-1173). - README.md (repository variable tables near line 108 and lines 296-301) | severity=low | confidence=4 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5] PROBLEM: Four new default-on repository variables (RETIRED_LABEL_DRAIN_ENABLED, SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_UNIFIED_ENABLED, ZOMBIE_RUN_REAPER_ENABLED, ZOMBIE_RUN_MAX_QUEUED_HOURS) are missing from README and docs; they appear only in docs/INVENTORY.md. WHY: Operators cannot find these rollback switches, and the retired-label drain closes open issues and PRs in every consumer repo that runs ai-sync-labels once this reaches stable. - scripts/ai_labels.py:1124 (`remaining_count = len(items) - processed_count`), consumed at 1132-1143 | severity=low | confidence=5 flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3] PROBLEM: processed_count goes up for every item the loop attempts, including items whose comment or close failed, so remaining_count counts only the items the budget never reached, not the items still open. WHY: With 3 open items where the first comment POST fails, the run logs `LABEL_SYNC_RETIRED_DRAIN_DEFERRED ... reason=item_failed remaining=0` while all 3 are still open, so the operator signal is wrong (the label is still kept correctly). - scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh:152-175 (cancel / force-cancel loop), fed by .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:356-364 | severity=low | confidence=3 flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3] PROBLEM: Run status is read once in the listing at the start of the sweep tick, and the run is cancelled later by id without re-checking. `POST /actions/runs/{id}/cancel` also succeeds on a run that has already started. WHY: A run that moved from queued to in_progress between the listing and the cancel is cancelled mid-execution, wasting one review cycle. The window is narrow because of the 24 h ZOMBIE_RUN_MAX_QUEUED_HOURS threshold. - scripts/review_autofix_sweep_reaper.sh:122-126 | severity=low | confidence=3 flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite] PROBLEM: The grep that pulls the status code out of the error log depends on gh's specific error format. WHY: If the gh error format changes or is localized, the reaper may miss 409 responses and fail to force-cancel stuck runs. minimax_minimax-m3 disputed this: the format dependency is only the fallback for the inline gh_api_retry shim, and the real helper sets GH_API_RETRY_LAST_STATUS. - scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3778-3783 | severity=low | confidence=3 flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite] PROBLEM: evaluate_failure_fingerprint_breaker catches all exceptions and returns a default "unavailable" decision. WHY: This hides bugs in the input data or the parsing logic, which makes breaker failures hard to debug. minimax_minimax-m3 disputed this as a deliberate fail-open (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3895-3896). === END CONSENSUS FINDINGS === === CONSENSUS TASK GAPS === - requirement: P3: the plan.yml and clarify.yml failure handlers compute `fingerprint = sha256(phase + failed_step_name + first ::error:: line normalized)[:12]` and append `` to the existing failure comment. Done when two identical plan-failure signatures across a planning↔clarification flip apply `ai:plan-failed` and enter the unblock judge. expected_change_site: .github/workflows/plan.yml "Comment on issue failure" (plan.yml:3400-3415) and the clarify.yml failure/blocked comment POST (clarify.yml:1863-1901), or a helper both call confidence=5 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash] EVIDENCE: AI_FAILURE_FINGERPRINT_V1 appears nowhere under .github/workflows/ or in any producer script; it appears only in the consumer (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3764-3766, scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:22536, :22709), in tests and in prose (README.md:3587, agents.d/stuck-states-p3b-stall-breaker.md:2, changelog.d/stuck-states-p3b-stall-breaker.md:2). The plan failure comment at plan.yml:3414-3415 is unchanged (workflow/issue/context/hint/run only), the clarify blocked comment at clarify.yml:1899-1900 has no marker, and plan.yml changes only at lines 105-111 (the CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_ALL_TEXT_ENABLED env row). The consumer is wired and on by default (orchestrate_poll.yml:1373) but can never trip. - requirement: P2a: replace the "Stage workflow support files" copy loop with the verified single source in clarify.yml, plan.yml and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml, and rewrite each `scripts/` invocation to `"${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/"`. expected_change_site: .github/workflows/plan.yml "Stage workflow support files" (plan.yml:584, copy loop at plan.yml:591) and its bare `source scripts/gh_helpers.sh` call sites; .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml "Stage workflow support files" (orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:481, copy loop at 489) and its call sites; the plan / clarify_respond arms of scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh; the PHASE_WORKFLOWS list in tests/test_support_script_single_source.py confidence=5 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash] EVIDENCE: scripts/stage_support_for_phase.sh:70-100 has only a clarify) arm, and its header (lines 6-8) defers plan, clarify_respond and implement. tests/test_support_script_single_source.py:43-46 lists only clarify.yml. plan.yml:591 and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml:489 still contain the `install -m 0755 "${src}" "scripts/${f}"` copy loop and still use bare script paths (e.g., scripts/gh_helpers.sh). z-ai_glm-5_3-flash also reports copy loops in .github/workflows/clarify.yml (lines 513, 538) and orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml (lines 498, 530). The heal-plan crash in run 37406961564 happens in plan.yml, which is still on the legacy loop. - requirement: P9: a `BLOCKED:` answer citing a path that `git ls-files` lists triggers one automatic re-clarify with the path listing appended, instead of `ai:blocked`. expected_change_site: .github/workflows/clarify.yml blocked-outcome step ("Handle blocked clarification output", clarify.yml:1863 / clarify.yml:1866-1901), scripts/clarify_blocked_verify.sh [new], tests/test_clarify_blocked_verify.py [new] confidence=5 flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash] EVIDENCE: Only the P9a snapshot half ships (scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh, CLARIFY_SNAPSHOT_ALL_TEXT_ENABLED). The blocked step still unconditionally runs `ensure_label_exists "ai:blocked"` (clarify.yml:1878-1883) and posts the existing comment (1899-1900); its only change is the `${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR:-scripts}` path rewrite. There is no retry marker, one-retry gate, git ls-files path verification or appended listing, and neither new file exists. - requirement: P2b: implement.yml runs every
